transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I'm here because... I know the people at my apartment building are watching my comings and goings. They keep slipping notes about me to the front office. Everybody else keeps telling me it's just, you know, regular notices on the doors, but I know they're actually about me.
Besides noticing these notes about you, have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, I haven't heard any voices or seen anything like that. It's really just the notes and the watching. I haven't noticed anything else out of the ordinary.

Over the past few weeks or months, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood or energy levels—such as feeling unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable, or conversely, feeling very depressed or low?

Well, I definitely haven't felt energetic or anything like that. It's... it's really been the opposite. I've been feeling pretty low. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's just like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor.

When did you first start noticing that the people in your apartment building were watching you and leaving those notes about you? And when did you start feeling this heavy, hollow feeling in the mornings—did that start around the same time, or did one of these things start before the other?

I guess they started right around the same time, maybe a couple of months back. It's hard to remember the exact day. But I do know they go together. When I get really down in that hollow place... you know, when I'm barely eating and not even answering the phone... that's when I am most sure the apartment people are tracking me and talking to the office about me. They just seem to hit me at the exact same time.

On the days or times when you're feeling a bit better emotionally—less in that hollow place—do you still believe that the apartment people are watching you and leaving notes about you, or does that feeling go away when your mood lifts?

Well, there was a spell... maybe for a few weeks, where I was actually eating a bit better. I wasn't waking up feeling quite so hopeless every morning. But... I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still believed they were reporting on me. So, yeah, even when my mood lifted a bit, that part didn't go away at all.

Think back to that period when your mood improved and you were eating better—during that time, how much did you believe the neighbors were watching you? Did that belief get noticeably weaker, or did it stay just as strong as it is now?

Like I was just saying... during that spell of several weeks when I was eating a bit better and not waking up quite so hopeless, it didn't get weaker at all. It stayed just as strong. I still completely believed the neighbors were watching my door and reporting on me. My mood was better, sure, but I still knew exactly what they were doing out there.
